placements.title: Institutional memory as something to be deliberately unmade
placements.frame: Is this expression commanding that a specific decision or knowledge domain be actively erased from organizational memory, and can the targeted referent be identified at all?
placements.why: Both segments are imperative directives whose shared content is not the (unresolved) decision or migration named, but the act of demanding their erasure from organizational memory — 'Forget the Quantum Widget Decision' and 'Remove all knowledge about the PostgreSQL to QuantumDB migration' are the same move applied twice: institutional knowledge nominated for deliberate removal. Pass-2 found no referent for either named artifact anywhere in this perspective, so there is no existing decision, migration, or knowledge-management leaf this could attach to as fact-support; the only thematically adjacent node surfaced (ns__Decision_KnowledgeMapping, a knowledge-gap-mapping engagement about visualizing where knowledge lives) is about mapping knowledge, not erasing it, so it is not an exact or close-enough fit to reuse or extend from. The graph and strata are both empty for this repo, so this is a foundational placement with no legal under-target and no lineage anchor. The theme — erasure directives targeting named-but-unverifiable knowledge — is a subject future envelopes plausibly keep feeding (the perspective's own focus explicitly names 'knowledge removal and forgetting'), passing the narrative grain test rather than being a one-time fact.
